items.prompt: Two browser tabs loaded the same workspace. Tab A renames page X and saves; a moment later Tab B, which never saw A's rename, edits page Y and saves. What does the server keep?
items.answer: Tab B's whole state: PUT replaces the entire workspace JSON, losing A's rename
distractors: Both edits, because the server merges the two saves page by page before writing
Tab A's state, because B's save is rejected as stale by a version check on PUT
Both edits, but the rename of page X is flagged as a conflict for the user to review
items.explanation: The route upserts the full state document; the SQL is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(workspace_id) DO UPDATE SET state_json = excluded.state_json. There is no version check or merge on the server.

items.prompt: A client PUTs a workspace whose meta.updatedAt is a date in the year 2099. What updatedAt is stored?
items.answer: The server's current time, which overwrites the client's meta.updatedAt
distractors: 2099, because the client's meta object is stored exactly as it was sent
The later of the client's timestamp and the server's own current time
None: the request is rejected with a 400 for carrying a future timestamp
items.explanation: nextState.meta is { ...(state.meta || {}), workspaceId, updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() }, so the route's later keys (updatedAt and workspaceId) win over the client's values.

items.prompt: applyRemoteState receives a remote state whose meta.updatedAt equals the local meta.updatedAt. What changes locally?
items.answer: Nothing: remote state is applied only when strictly newer than local
distractors: Everything: remote state always replaces local state when it arrives
Only pages and blocks are replaced, while local comments are kept
The remote state is merged key by key into the local workspace state
items.explanation: The guard returns {} when remoteUpdatedAt <= localUpdatedAt (or is NaN). When it is newer, collections are replaced wholesale, not merged.

items.prompt: A PUT /api/workspace arrives whose state.activities already holds 200 entries. How many activities are stored afterwards, and which one is dropped?
items.answer: 200: the new activity is appended and slice(-200) drops the oldest
distractors: 201: the log is appended to and grows without any upper bound at all
200: the new activity is discarded, because the log is already full
1: the log is reset to just the new entry once it reaches 200 items
items.explanation: activities is [...existing, newEntry].slice(-200): keep the last 200, i.e. the newest, so the oldest entry is the one dropped.

items.prompt: Page A contains B, and B contains C. A user drags A onto C (movePage(A, C)). What happens?
items.answer: Nothing: walking up from C reaches A, so the move is refused as a cycle
distractors: A moves under C, and C is promoted to become the new root of the tree
A moves under C, and B is re-parented to the root to break the cycle
It throws a cycle error, and the sidebar shows an error toast to the user
items.explanation: isDescendant(pages, C, A) follows parentId links from C: C -> B -> A, finds A, returns true, so movePage returns no changes. movePage also ignores moving a page onto itself.

items.prompt: Parent page P is soft-deleted but its child page Q is not. Does Q appear in the sidebar tree built by buildPageTree?
items.answer: No: the recursion only descends through pages that are not deleted
distractors: Yes, promoted to the root level until its parent page is restored
Yes, still nested under P, which is shown greyed out in the tree
Yes, because Q's own isDeleted flag is false, so the filter keeps it
items.explanation: Each level filters parentId === parentId && !isDeleted and recurses into the survivors only. Q stays in pages but is unreachable from the visible tree while P is in the trash.

items.prompt: recent is [B, A, C] and the user opens page A. What is recent afterwards?
items.answer: [A, B, C]: A moves to the front and its old entry is removed
distractors: [A, B, A, C]: every visit is recorded, including repeat visits
[B, A, C]: pages already in the list keep their current position
[B, C, A]: the old entry is removed and the visit goes to the end
items.explanation: [pageId, ...state.recent.filter((id) => id !== pageId)].slice(0, 40): a move-to-front, deduplicated list capped at 40.

items.prompt: addBlock is called with an afterBlockId that no longer exists on the page. Where is the new block inserted?
items.answer: At the end of the page, since findIndex returns -1 and index < 0 pushes
distractors: At the start of the page, since the -1 index plus 1 splices at position 0
Nowhere: the call is ignored because the anchor block cannot be found
Right after the first block of the page, as the fallback anchor block
items.explanation: Both an unknown afterBlockId and the last block's id lead to list.push; only a found, non-last index uses splice(index + 1, 0, nextBlock).

items.prompt: PATCH /api/workspace/version restores a version of page X. What does it change in the stored workspace?
items.answer: It overlays X with the snapshot page and blocks, and bumps meta.updatedAt
distractors: It rolls the whole workspace back to the moment the version was saved
It restores only X's title from the snapshot and leaves its blocks as is
It creates a new page from the snapshot and places it next to page X
items.explanation: It rewrites state.pages[pageIndex] (spread with version.snapshot.page) and replaces state.blocksByPage[pageId] with the snapshot blocks, then upserts the workspace with a new updatedAt. Other pages are untouched.

items.prompt: With default arguments, how stale may a presence entry and a typing indicator become before the prune functions drop them?
items.answer: Presence up to 13000 ms, typing indicators up to 3000 ms
distractors: Both presence and typing indicators up to 13000 ms
Typing indicators outlive presence: 13000 ms against 3000 ms
Both survive until the page is reloaded or the tab closes
items.explanation: prunePresence(maxAgeMs = 13000) and pruneTyping(maxAgeMs = 3000) keep entries whose now - updatedAt <= maxAgeMs.

items.front: In updateBlock, what happens to block.props when the patch contains props, and when it does not?
items.back: With patch.props the old and new props are shallow-merged ({ ...block.props, ...patch.props }); without it the existing props are kept even though the rest of the patch is spread over the block.

items.front: Which IndexedDB object stores does the offline layer use, and in what order is the sync queue replayed?
items.back: Database notion-clone-offline holds syncQueue and drafts. readSyncQueue returns queued items sorted by createdAt ascending - oldest first.

items.front: When savePageVersion snapshots a page, where does the snapshot's content come from?
items.back: From the workspace state already stored on the server (getWorkspaceState), not from the client's in-memory edits - unsaved changes are not in the version.
